style: Say brightly and clearly, like an upbeat tour guide
lines: Tap a button in Questions to collect a clue before making a claim.
You have every clue. Tap Make a claim to choose a cause and prove it.
Welcome to the help desk. A caller can't get online. Tap a question to ask it. Each answer lights up part of their house.
Tap a question to ask the caller. Then tap Make a claim.
Tap the cause you think it is. Then tap one or two clues that prove it, and press Send fix.
That clue doesn't prove a cause yet. Tap a clue that shows what is broken.
The caller tried that, and it still doesn't work. Ask another question, or check your clues.
Solved. It was a connection problem: the path was broken.
Solved. It was a logging in problem: the device had to prove who it was.
Solved. It was a permission problem: logging in worked, but that account isn't allowed. That's on purpose.
Tap Next call, or a phone on the call strip.
That's every call. Look at your shift report: which questions found the problem fastest?
This is a house you can change. Tap a device, change something, then try the internet, a website or the printer.
No bars. Walls and distance weaken Wi-Fi. Drag the tablet closer to the router.
Tap Shift report to compare all eight calls.
Tap Start a new shift to take the calls again, or tap Open House to explore.
Tap a device, change its controls, then tap a button in Try. Drag the tablet or move it with arrow keys.
Watch the fix and test ping. You can tap another phone on the call strip to change calls.
Tap Back to questions to ask more, or choose another cause and clues, then press Send fix.
What kind of problem is it? Tap Connection, Logging in or Permission.
Look at your clues again. Is the path broken, did logging in fail, or did it work?
